note: Australia, read in the statutes on the Federal Register of Legislation: the Migration Regulations 1994 (compilation 289, in force 2 October 2026), the Migration Act 1958 (compilation 172, in force 8 October 2026) and the Australian Citizenship Act 2007 (as in force 4 June 2026); the Department of Home Affairs' visa pages answered this client with their content only in scripts and a rendering of them was refused (403), so its processing times aren't read. The National Innovation visa (subclass 858, the former Distinguished Talent and Global Talent visa) is a permanent visa, by invitation, for one with an internationally recognised record of exceptional and outstanding achievement in a profession, a sport, the arts or academia and research, still prominent in it; it is applied for in or outside Australia; its first instalment is AUD 6,235 (AUD 5,110 for a Pacific-regional passport holder), and a second instalment of AUD 4,890 is asked of some applicants (the English-language case), which the form doesn't hold; being permanent, it has no term and lets its holder work freely. The Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) is a temporary visa on an employer's nomination (work for the sponsor), lasting the period of stay proposed in the nomination (no fixed term in the Regulations, so none kept), AUD 4,015 (AUD 3,290 Pacific-regional), applied for in or outside Australia. New Zealand citizens holding a New Zealand passport in force get a special category visa (Migration Act section 32), on arrival. Citizenship by conferral asks four years' presence in Australia, never as an unlawful non-citizen, the last twelve months as a permanent resident (section 22), so lawful years on each of these count. Permanent residence by other routes (employer nomination, skilled independent) and the second instalment aren't written.

sources.title: Australian Citizenship Act 2007 (as in force 4 June 2026), section 22
sources.said: (a) the person was present in Australia for the period of 4 years immediately before the day the person made the application; and (b) the person was not present in Australia as an unlawful non-citizen at any time during that 4 year period; and (c) the person was present in Australia as a permanent resident for the period of 12 months immediately before the day the person made the application.
